title: Effects of different thickening agents on infant gut microbiota
authors: González-Bermúdez CA, López-Nicolás R, Peso-Echarri P, Frontela-Saseta C, Martínez-Graciá C
population: Fresh faecal samples from healthy donors aged 2 to 3 months
funder: Funding statement not read: the article is closed access and absent from PubMed Central, the publisher's full text returned an automated-access challenge (HTTP 403), and the archived copy holds only the landing page. Publisher-deposited Crossref metadata name Fundación Séneca (award 11978/PI/09) and Universidad de Murcia.
result: Batch fermentation with 1% (w/v) locust bean gum, maize hydroxypropylated distarch phosphate or pre-gelatinised rice starch. Both starches gave lower pH than locust bean gum (p < 0.01) and higher total gas production (p < 0.05); total short-chain fatty acids and propionate were higher with locust bean gum (p < 0.05). The starches induced higher Lactobacillus and Bifidobacteria at the beginning of fermentation, a sudden drop of pH and greater acetate production, which promoted a less varied faecal microbiota; locust bean gum promoted a more varied microbiota. Results read from the PubMed abstract.
